action: urlscan notes that at least one kit persists in theme and plugin files on disk, so review those files; it says cleaning up one injection does not mean the threat has been mitigated.
date_note: Date of the urlscan post; the page gives no earlier day for the compromise.
exec: A compromised WordPress site carried 13 ClickFix injections, which trick visitors into running malware themselves.
geo_basis: site owner and country not stated; global
plain: urlscan's researchers say one hacked WordPress site carried 13 ClickFix traps, fake checks that get visitors to run malicious commands, planted by three different kits.
summary: The urlscan Threat Research Team says in a 19 November post that a single compromised WordPress site carried 13 ClickFix injections from three distinct kits. It says some used EtherHiding, which takes next-stage server addresses from Polygon smart contracts, and that competing loaders interfered with each other. Cyber Press relays the report.
title: urlscan finds 13 ClickFix injections from three kits on one compromised WordPress site

validation.note: urlscan's own report (primary, investigating firm) read in full; Cyber Press (23 Nov) relays it. urlscan names the compromised site (academicpipelinedatabase[.]net, defanged) but gives no organisation or country, so the event is placed globally.

evidence.quote: carrying thirteen separate ClickFix injections from three distinct kits
Security researchers found 13 ClickFix injections on a single compromised WordPress site

review.note: validation note wrongly said no victim site is named (urlscan names the compromised site); note and geo_basis fixed; title, 13 injections/3 kits, EtherHiding, date and action match urlscan
